summary: Specifies the DetNet YANG data model for configuration and operational data of DetNet flows. It allows provisioning an end-to-end DetNet service along the path without a signaling protocol, and conforms to NMDA.

eli5.summary: This is a standard settings form for devices on a promised-delivery-time network, plus a status page.

questions: what is the detnet yang model
what are detnet service and forwarding sub-layers
subtitle: A standard YANG model for configuring DetNet flows and reading their status, with no signaling protocol needed.

tldr.problem: Deterministic Networking (DetNet) carries real-time flows with bounded latency and very low loss, but devices along a path need a common way to be configured and to report flow status.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9633 defines the ietf-detnet YANG module. It models App-flows, a service sub-layer and a forwarding sub-layer, all pointing at shared traffic profiles, and supports aggregation of flows.
tldr.outcome: A controller or operator can provision an end-to-end DetNet service on every device along the path without depending on a signaling protocol. The module conforms to NMDA.

today: RFC 9633 is a Proposed Standard published in October 2024 and has not been obsoleted or updated. IANA has registered the ietf-detnet namespace and YANG module name.

sections.title: What the DetNet YANG Model Is For
sections.content:
DetNet (Deterministic Networking) carries specified unicast or multicast data flows for real-time applications with extremely low packet loss rates and an assured maximum end-to-end delivery latency. Background and concepts are in RFC 8655.

This RFC defines a YANG data model, built on the types and language of RFC 6991 and RFC 7950. It covers the DetNet service, which describes what is offered to application flows, and DetNet configuration: flow path set-up, flow status reporting and configuration of DetNet functions, aimed at end-to-end bounded latency and zero congestion loss.

The model is scoped to aggregation, disaggregation and the data plane capabilities of the DetNet data planes in RFC 8655 and RFC 8938. DetNet operates at the IP layer and delivers service over lower-layer technologies such as MPLS and IEEE 802.1 Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN).
sections.eli5: Some messages must arrive on time, like a train that may never be late. This is the common form that tells every station how to handle those messages.

sections.title: Layers and Node Types
sections.content:
The module has three kinds of layer: the App-flow data layer, the service sub-layer and the forwarding sub-layer. Traffic parameters live in a separate traffic profile that any layer can reference. A profile can be shared, and it lists the members currently using it.

Which layers a device has depends on its node type for a given service. An edge node has all three layers. A relay node has the service and forwarding sub-layers. A transit node has only the forwarding sub-layer. Node types are logical roles per DetNet service, so one device may be an edge node for one service and a different type for another.

Every layer has ingress/incoming and egress/outgoing operations, though an instance may be unidirectional only. The model is controller-based: a controller or operator configures all the devices that form a service.
sections.eli5: Think of a parcel service: the sender's desk (App-flow), the sorting depot (service), and the roads between depots (forwarding). Small stops only need the roads.

sections.title: What Each Layer Configures
sections.content:
The App-flow layer maps application flows, Layer 2 or Layer 3, to DetNet flows at the edge. Flow mapping at the User-Network Interface uses the attributes of RFC 9016.

The service sub-layer provides functions such as DetNet tunnel initialization and termination and service protection. Its attributes include flow identification and the service function type, and a service-rank plus an operation of initiation, termination, relay or non-detnet.

The forwarding sub-layer provides optional congestion protection and explicit routes, which avoid interruptions caused by routing or bridging convergence. For MPLS it uses operations such as impose-and-forward, swap-and-forward and pop-and-lookup. The model programs the data plane, so existing explicit route mechanisms can be reused. It provides data plane configuration of IP addresses or MPLS labels, but no control plane mapping.

The traffic profile holds requirements such as min-bandwidth, max-latency, max-latency-variation, max-loss, max-consecutive-loss-tolerance and max-misordering, plus a traffic specification of the flow.
sections.eli5: Each layer has its own few boxes to fill in. One shared page says how fast, how reliable and how steady the delivery needs to be.

sections.title: Service Protection and Sequence Numbers
sections.content:
The service sub-layer can protect a flow with the DetNet packet functions, selected by the service-protection setting. replication is the Packet Replication Function (PRF), which copies packets to one or more next hops. elimination is the Packet Elimination Function (PEF), which removes duplicates. ordering is the Packet Ordering Function (POF), which reorders packets received out of order. Combined values such as elimination-ordering-replication are also defined, and none means no protection.

Sequence numbers are configured too. The sequence number field can be unused (zero-sn), 16 bits (short-sn) or 28 bits (long-sn). The sequence number can be copied from the App-flow (copy-from-app-flow) or generated for the DetNet flow at the ingress (generate-by-detnet-flow). The module warns that, with generation, there must be only one source of sequence numbers.
sections.eli5: To be safe, a message can be sent along two roads at once. Numbering the copies lets the receiver throw away the second one and keep things in order.

sections.title: Flow Aggregation
sections.content:
DetNet flow aggregation improves the scalability of the data, management and control planes, because some nodes can treat an aggregate as a single DetNet flow. Aggregated flows should be compatible. A bandwidth reservation should reasonably represent the total aggregate, and the total delay should not exceed the maximum delay bound of any individual flow.

The model supports aggregate encapsulation, decapsulation and identification, mapping individual flows to an aggregate, and changing traffic specification parameters for aggregates. Eight scenarios are listed: ingress nodes aggregating App-flows into a service sub-layer, or service sub-layers into a forwarding sub-layer or an aggregate service sub-layer; relay nodes aggregating forwarding or service sub-layers into either kind of sub-layer; and transit nodes aggregating forwarding sub-layers. Reserving resources and tracking services inside an aggregate are out of scope.
sections.eli5: Instead of tracking every car, you track a whole bus. It is easier to manage, as long as the bus is at least as fast as its slowest rider needs.

sections.title: The Module and Its Examples
sections.content:
The module is ietf-detnet, with prefix dnet, revision 2024-10-28 and namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-detnet. It imports types from RFC 6991, RFC 8519, RFC 8294, RFC 8343 and IEEE 802.1Q-2022, and it conforms to NMDA. Its top-level container is detnet, holding traffic-profile, app-flows, service and forwarding.

Appendix A gives the complete YANG tree. Appendix B has JSON examples of operational data for aggregation cases: App-flows into one service sub-layer (A-1), aggregation using a forwarding sub-layer (B-1), service aggregation (B-2), relay service sub-layer cases (C-1 to C-4) and transit node forwarding aggregation (D-1).
sections.eli5: The rest of the RFC is the actual form, written in a strict computer-readable format, with sample filled-in forms for different set-ups.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
General DetNet security is covered in RFC 8655 and RFC 9055. The module is meant to be accessed with NETCONF (RFC 6241, over SSH) or RESTCONF (RFC 8040, over TLS), and access can be restricted with NACM (RFC 8341).

The writable data nodes are sensitive. Unauthorized writes can break or incorrectly connect DetNet flows, and because DetNet is a configured data plane, changes not coordinated with all devices on the path cause denial of service. An attacker could also redirect a path so traffic avoids inspection or passes an adversary node.

Readable nodes can leak information too. /detnet/app-flows and the traffic profile membership can reveal characteristics of application flows, while the service and forwarding sub-layer nodes can reveal aspects of the network topology.
sections.eli5: Whoever can change the settings can break the schedule or send things down a bad road, so only trusted people should be allowed to, or even to peek at them.
